questions.q: How does the summary say relationships differ from cake?
a: They grow stronger the more you use them
They shrink each time you share them
They spoil if kept too long
They need the same recipe every time
questions.why: Lesson 1 compares relationships to muscles: the more you exercise them, the stronger they become.

questions.q: What question does a good networker ask instead of how others can help?
a: How can I help others?
Who can I meet next?
What can I get in return?
Why should I bother?
questions.why: Lesson 1 ends by advising networkers to ask how they can help others rather than how others can help them.

questions.q: Why is it important to build your network before you need it?
a: Trust built early makes help available later
Contacts expire after a few years
Employers only hire people they know
Networking events are cheaper in advance
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a foundation of trust means you can count on help when a problem eventually arrives.

questions.q: What did Bill Clinton do as a young man to build relationships?
a: He wrote down the names of everyone he met each day
He hosted a weekly dinner for strangers
He sent birthday cards to every voter
He kept a list of favors he was owed
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Clinton, at 22, wrote down everyone he had met that day so he would remember them.

questions.q: What does Keith mean by relationship glue?
a: Shared experiences that turn acquaintances into friends
A script for making small talk at events
A system for tracking thousands of contacts
Gifts sent on birthdays and holidays
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes relationship glue as things like a hard climb or a long midnight talk that create real friendship.
